title:
Cell Patterning on Photolithographically Defined 
Parylene-C: SiO2 Substrates
protocol: Design desired parylene-C configuration using layout editor software capable of reading CIF or GDS-II files.
Commission photo mask manufacture to an appropriate microelectronics facility, or make in-house if facilities exist.
Oxidize a silicon wafer in an atmospheric horizontal furnace at 950 °C for 40 min to produce a 200 nm SiO2 layer.
Prime the oxidized wafer with silane adhesion promoter.
Deposit parylene-C at 22 °C using a vacuum deposition system designed for parylene, at a rate of 1.298 nm/mg of dimer.
Spin the wafer at 4000 rpm for 30 sec whilst applying positive photo-resist to achieve a theoretical thickness of 1 μm.
Soft bake the wafer for 60 sec at 90 °C.
Insert both the wafer and premanufactured photo mask into a mask aligner.
Expose the photoresist-coated wafer with UV negative representation of the desired parylene-C configuration.
Bake exposed wafer for 60 sec at 110 °C.
Remove photo-resist from the wafer by developing in an appropriate developer solution.
Etch off the unprotected parylene using an oxygen plasma etch system.
Reveal the underlying SiO2 by etching with an oxygen plasma etch system.
Dice the wafer using a dicing saw (spindle speed 30,000 rpm, feed speed 7 mm/sec).
Rinse chips in deionized H2O and blow dry with nitrogen.
Store chips indefinitely in dust-free boxes until required.
Remove residual photoresist from chips by washing in acetone for 10 sec.
Rinse chips three times in deionized distilled H2O.
Mix fresh piranha acid (a 5:3 ratio of 30% hydrogen peroxide and 98% sulfuric acid).
Clean and etch chips by immersing them in piranha acid for 10 min.
Rinse chips three times in deionized H2O.
Transfer chips to a sterile culture dish.
Activate chips for cell patterning under sterile conditions in a laminar flow tissue culture hood.
Add two chips per well to a 6-well plate.
Add 2 ml of fetal bovine serum to fully immerse all chips.
Incubate chips in serum for 3-12 hours at 37 °C.
Remove chips from activation solution and wash once for 10 seconds in Hank's Balanced Salt Solution.
Place chip in a culture well.
Plate chosen cell type as a suspension in its usual growth media.
Use a density of 5 x 10^4 cells/ml as a starting point for optimum plating density.
